basis: Primary focal or segmental dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; affected muscle groups do not imply primary muscle damage.

Hypotrichosis, intellectual disability and syndactyly define the syndrome; early tooth eruption alone does not establish dental damage.

Neoplasm occupying the pineal body, an endocrine gland within the brain; both brain and endocrine neoplasm ancestors support these axes.

Triglyceride storage directly damages myocardium and coronary arteries; skeletal myopathy occurs in 80-99%. Leukocyte vacuoles alone do not imply blood dysfunction.
Progressive carpotarsal osteolysis; renal insufficiency occurs in 15/19 and corneal opacity in 3/9, the latter just above the involvement threshold.

Adipocytic soft-tissue sarcoma, typically arising in deep soft tissues; no specific visceral or cutaneous origin is established.
Mitochondrial myopathy with ophthalmoplegia; cerebellar atrophy, ataxia and neuropathy reported in 1/1. Cardiac and hearing abnormalities omitted by cap.
Spondyloepiphyseal skeletal dysplasia; listed CNS, palatal and ocular abnormalities lack frequency evidence sufficient for additional involvement.
Lethal skeletal dysplasia with abnormal ossification and bowed limbs; lung aplasia/hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. Abnormal GH testing alone is insufficient.
Autoimmune inflammation of the optic nerve, which belongs to the ocular axis; no additional nervous system involvement is established.
